newsitem.title: USA: Cone Mills sees Q2 hurt by high inventories.
newsitem.headline: Cone Mills sees Q2 hurt by high inventories.

text.p: Cone Mills said Thursday that even though it has seen some improvement in both denim and specialty sportswear markets, it believes that second quarter results will continue to be hurt by curtailed manufacturing operating schedules as it reduces inventories.

J. Patrick Danahy, president and chief executive officer, said "Even though first quarter results were disappointing, they were generally in line with our expectations. We continued to experience value-added denim inventory adjustments in certain customer segments and weak fashion demand for decorative prints."

He added, however, that the company is making progress with its program to return the company to profitability by focuisng on its core businesses, aggressive marketing, cost reduction, the reconfiguration of manufacturing operations and capital conservation.
Cone recorded a loss in the first quarter, ended March 30, of almost $2 million, or $0.10 a share fully-diluted.
